transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this planning roundtable. As you know, we have a proposed six-week peer-tutoring program for grades 6 through 8 on the table, and before I sign off on it, I want to make sure we've thoroughly considered all the operational details. The draft currently calls for two adult supervisors, Google Classroom for session communication, student-selected tutor pairings, and paper consent forms. I'd like to go around the table and hear from each of you about any concerns or considerations related to your area of expertise. Let's start with whatever you think is most important for me to know before I set the operating requirements.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag an important staffing issue. I received the finalized roster from the activities office yesterday, and it contains 18 student tutors. The school's supervision rule permits one adult to supervise no more than six tutors in an active tutoring session. That means with 18 tutors, we'd need at least three adult supervisors, not two. The draft plan still lists the preliminary staffing estimate of two supervisors, which would be insufficient under the current supervision rule.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical concern about the student-selected tutor pairings. I completed a student-support review this week, and it revealed two active no-contact restrictions involving prospective tutors and students who are seeking tutoring. These restrictions are currently recorded only in confidential counseling files, so no one else here would have been aware of them. Because of these restrictions, tutor pairings cannot be left to student self-selection — they must be assigned and monitored by me as counselor to ensure we don't inadvertently place students together in violation of those no-contact orders. I'd recommend that the operating requirements specify counselor-assigned pairings rather than student-selected ones.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technology issue with the draft plan. Google Classroom is not approved for this program's student-to-student communication. The district-managed Microsoft Teams education environment is the approved platform, and it retains the required school records. I confirmed the platform settings with district IT this week, but the technology field in the draft application still lists Google Classroom and has not been updated. Before Dr. Singh sets the operating requirements, the plan needs to be corrected to specify Microsoft Teams as the communication platform.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag an important issue with the consent process described in the draft. I confirmed with the family-engagement office this week that for this program, family consent must be entered into the student information system before a student can participate. The district has also approved translated electronic consent forms in addition to paper forms. However, the draft plan still only describes paper form collection without any SIS entry requirement. Before you set the operating requirements, Dr. Singh, the consent procedure needs to be updated to include SIS entry and to make the translated electronic forms available to families.
